conviction_note: The facts lean slightly positive: H1 operating profit will clear the company's H1 plan, which the June/July/August monthly sales already show, and management promised a full-year revisit plus a real-estate plan at this print. The full-year bar the market holds, though, is the IFIS consensus (OP 60.8bn, ordinary 61.7bn), already 6-8% above the company plan. A raise that passes through the H1 beat lands at or just under it. This name fell the next day after 5 of its last 8 prints, including both H1 prints that came with an upward revision and a dividend raise. So the findings sum to +0.40 while the scaled number is -0.19 (p_up 47 on abs 3.2): the gap is the reaction function overriding a mildly positive fundamental read.
bar: Market bar: IFIS consensus for FY2027/2 OP 60,800m and ordinary 61,700m, unchanged for 4 weeks (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=8233, read 2026-10-14/15), against the company plan of OP 57,500m / ordinary 57,000m / NP 38,000m / dividend 40 yen (H1 plan OP 26,400m), unrevised since 2026-04-14 (https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260630/140120260624579151.pdf). There is no sourced H1 consensus. print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of the revised FY OP guide (~60.0bn) against the 60.8bn consensus.
positioning_check: JPX short register: no disclosed position at or above 0.5% as of 2026-10-14 (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html), so a real zero and nothing building. 信用倍率 2.62 on kabutan 2026-10-15 (irbank showed 3.55 on 7/17), so margin longs are moderately crowded and still unwinding. No options, so no skew. Baseline priced_lean -0.32 (margin overhang -0.21, run-up -0.11). Tape: down ~16% from the 2,503.5 close on the Q1 print day (2026-06-30) to 2,110 on 10/14, after a -1.95% day on 10/14 in sympathy with J.Front's H1. Up ~2% intraday on 10/15 (2,152.5 at 10:14 JST per kabuyoho).

findings.finding: H1 operating profit will beat the company's 26.4bn H1 plan, probably by about 7-10%. Q1 OP was 15,971m, 68.4% of the H1 plan, against 52.3% and 59.0% at the same point in the two prior years, so Q2 only needs ~10.4bn against 11.0bn a year ago. Q2 department-store sales then ran +2.3% (June; +5.8% underlying after a May/June booking shift), +7.4% (July) and +3.9% (August).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-30) printed OP +26.4% YoY, about 1bn above the internal plan, and the stock fell 2.34% the next day. The H1 FY26 print (2025-10-14) beat its H1 ordinary plan and fell 2.87%. This name sells visible beats.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The monthly series and the Q1 progress rate are public, and the consensus already sits above plan. Only the precise size of the beat is new. If the market doubted the beat, consensus would not sit 6-8% above the company plan.
findings.independence: The monthly reports are separate documents: https://www.release.tdnet.info/inbs/140120260904532165.pdf (Aug, 2026-09-15), https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260817/140120260807515733.pdf (Jul), https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260715/140120260713592606.pdf (Jun).

findings.finding: At the Q1 call management said it would revisit the full-year plan at this H1 print, and said inbound upside to the 845億 plan was more likely if FX held (Sept 1-14 duty-free sales +23.0%). Even so, a revision that passes through roughly the H1 beat (~+2-2.5bn, as last year's H1 raise of 50.0 to 52.5bn did) lands at about 60bn OP. That is at or just under the 60.8bn consensus, with the H2 caveat being the November 2026 switch of the tax-free system to refunds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-14 H1: FY OP raised 50.0 to 52.5bn with a dividend raise; next close -2.87%. 2024-10-15 H1: revision plus dividend raise plus buyback; next close -1.39%. 2026-01-06: forecast raise plus CB buyback/cancellation; next close +9.47%, the only large positive, and it came with a capital action.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction of the revision is expected: consensus at 60.8/61.7 against a plan of 57.5/57.0 shows the street has already raised. What is not priced is the decision itself: whether management passes through the full H1 beat plus inbound upside (beating consensus) or holds H2 for the tax-free change and FX (missing it). That is new on the day. If the market expected a conservative hold, consensus would sit at plan.
findings.independence: Consensus level: https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=8233 (2026-10-14). Last year's revision size: https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20251014/140120251013572278.pdf. Tax-free change flagged as the sector overhang: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=3099&b=n202610060612 (2026-10-06).

findings.finding: A dividend raise with the H1 results is likely. The company's stated policy is a ~30% payout (FY dividend 40 yen on 129.7 yen EPS), and it raised the dividend at both prior H1 prints (2024-10-15 and 2025-10-14, the latter to 17+17). Any net-profit raise therefore maps mechanically to a higher year-end dividend. No buyback is in the FY2026 plan, and leverage rose after the 130bn CB buyback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both prior H1 dividend raises were followed by down days (-1.39%, -2.87%). The ex-ante expectation of a raise is high, so a raise alone is small.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a habit. What is new is only the size: a raise above ~2-3 yen, or a buyback, would be a surprise. A priced buyback expectation would show up as the stock holding up into the print, but it fell 16% from June.

findings.finding: At the Q1 call management promised to present at this H1 print a fundamental reform plan for low-ROIC store properties, explicitly premised on keeping ownership. It is a new item on a register where the Murakami-linked City Index Eleventh still held 3.66% at the end of February 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of this line. Capital-policy news (the 2026-01-06 CB buyback) moved the stock +9.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Its content is unknown until the release. The 'retain ownership' premise has been public since July, so a disposal-driven re-rating is not expected. A concrete ROIC/ROE path is the upside. The stock's slide since July shows no anticipation of a capital-policy catalyst.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 2, but a different item in it. Activist holder record: https://irbank.net/8233/holder (as of the Feb 2026 register).

findings.finding: Peer J.Front's H1 (10/13 15:30) showed OP -10.5% on the Expo comp and the Daimaru Umeda renovation, and Takashimaya fell 1.95% on 10/14 in sympathy. Takashimaya's own Q2 domestic sales grew in every month, though its Osaka store was only +0.4% in August, so the Expo comp touches it too.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history for peer read-through.
findings.why_not_priced: A sympathy drop on a peer whose shortfall is largely idiosyncratic can unwind when the name's own numbers land. But the stock is already up ~2% intraday on 10/15, so much of it may have reversed before entry.

outside_window.finding: Japan's tax-free system changes to a refund model from November 2026. The effect on Takashimaya's inbound sales (FY plan 845億) shows in the November-December monthly reports, after the window. Only the company's commentary on it lands inside the window, and that is filed under finding 2.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: very likely (management said at Q1 it would re-present the FY plan at H1); the bar is consensus OP 60.8bn / ordinary 61.7bn against plan 57.5/57.0. Returns: dividend raise likely by the 30% payout rule and the two prior H1 precedents; no buyback planned. New-year guide: n/a (H1). Quarter vs own 進捗率: Q1 OP was 68.4% of H1 plan against 52-59% in prior years, and Q2 sales were up every month, so H1 OP lands ~27.5-29bn against 26.4bn planned; this is visible and priced.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Bond shelf resolution of up to 50bn (domestic unsecured, ≤4.0%, ≤10y) approved 2026-06-30
rejected_candidates.detail: This is refinancing of the borrowings used for the CB buyback, already reflected in the leverage context of finding 3. It buys nothing new that bears on this print.

baseline_tension: Positioning (-0.32 lean, margin ratio 2.62, no disclosed shorts) and the name's habit of falling after prints agree with a slight negative. The strongest positives the release could carry, all looked for: an FY raise above consensus on inbound upside (Sept duty-free +23%), a dividend raise, a real-estate/ROIC plan, or a surprise buyback, against a stock already down 16% since June on tax-free/FX worries. Those keep p_up near 50 rather than in the 30s.
lessons_applied: nothing changed: rule 1 (negatives resting on public 月次/進捗率) does not touch the one negative finding, which is about the forecast decision the release adds rather than a visible miss, and the visible H1 beat was already sized small; rule 2 (check the sign, look for positives) was already met because the dividend, real-estate plan and inbound-upside positives were searched and filed, so p_up stays 47 and every size is unchanged
